title: Separate affordances from signifiers
principle: Don Norman (DOET revised, public TOC/notes on jnd.org): affordances are possible actions; signifiers communicate where the action is. AI UIs often decorate without clarifying action—fix for discoverability: can a new user tell what to do?
procedure: List intended actions on the view.
For each, name the affordance (what’s possible) and the signifier (how it’s shown).
Remove decoration that looks actionable but isn’t; strengthen weak signifiers.
Check mapping: control layout should match cause→effect.
Provide feedback so the gulfs of execution/evaluation shrink.
examplePrompts:
Audit this UI with Norman’s affordances vs signifiers (DOET / jnd.org public notes):
- Table: action → affordance → signifier → feedback.
- Flag false affordances (looks clickable, isn’t).
- Propose stronger signifiers without adding chrome noise.
No endorsement.
